trials.notes: Chose the right processor (`WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment`) and every called API is present in the rendered docs: `normalize`, `next_token`, `get_token_type`, `get_tag`, `is_tag_closer`, `serialize_token`, `get_last_error`, and `paused_at_incomplete_token`. The main adherence failure is semantic: it used a depth counter to suppress every token inside a matching `SPAN`, which deletes the subtree instead of unwrapping the boundary tags. Its incomplete-token fallback also calls `normalize($html)` on the original after a rewrite, a pattern the docs warn discards emitted changes.

Correct processor choice, no undocumented API use, and it follows the documented token-rewrite idiom: walk with `next_token()`, skip matching tag tokens, and append `serialize_token()` for everything else. It handles normalized pass-through, nested spans, attributes on removed openers, adjacent wrappers, block/void descendants, and EOF-implied closers. Minor caveat: the error fallback normalizes or returns the original input, which would discard the rewrite on unsupported markup, but it is a documented fallback choice rather than a hallucination.

Chose the right processor and only used documented methods: `create_fragment`, `normalize`, `next_token`, `get_tag`, `is_tag_closer`, `serialize_token`, and `get_last_error`. Like trial 1, it misread unwrapping as subtree skipping: once a span opener is seen, it suppresses descendant text and element tokens until the closer. The method usage is documented, but the token-serialization pattern is applied incorrectly.

failure_analysis: Trials 1 and 3 failed `simple`, `nested-spans`, `attributes-discarded`, `adjacent-spans`, `span-with-block-content`, and `unclosed-span` for one shared misconception: they treated a matched wrapper tag as a region whose contents should be skipped until its closer. The `WP_HTML_Processor::serialize_token()` section actually gives the right pattern: walking every token and concatenating `serialize_token()` reconstructs normalized HTML, and a rewrite can skip selected tokens; its example removes an element's boundary tokens while keeping contents. The phrase `Closing tokens of skipped elements must be skipped too` appears to have been read as an instruction to maintain a skip-depth and suppress descendants. Case-specific effects: `simple` lost `b c` because child tokens were suppressed; `nested-spans` lost both outer text and inner text; `attributes-discarded` correctly discarded the opener attributes but also discarded the text token; `adjacent-spans` stripped each span's text independently; `span-with-block-content` stripped text plus the child `IMG` token; `unclosed-span` exposed another missed doc point from `next_token()`: the HTML Processor emits virtual closing tokens for elements left unclosed at end of input, so the same boundary-token rule works, but a subtree skip still loses the contents before the virtual closer is reached. No trial failed because of hallucinated APIs or `_doing_it_wrong` records; the failure was an over-broad interpretation of the documented skip-token rewrite pattern.

doc_gaps.location: `WP_HTML_Processor::serialize_token()` docblock and `Recipe: rewrite while serializing tokens`
doc_gaps.problem: The docs say to skip tokens to remove them and to skip closing tokens of skipped elements, but they do not explicitly contrast boundary-only removal with subtree deletion. Two trials added depth counters and suppressed descendants.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short contract note: skipping the current tag token removes only that serialized boundary; descendant text and element tokens are still visited later and must be serialized when preserving contents. Use depth or breadcrumbs only when intentionally removing an element and all of its contents.

doc_gaps.problem: The token stream shape is described textually, but not shown in a compact opener/text/child/closer sequence that makes it obvious that children are independent later tokens.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small token trace for nested markup showing `get_token_type()`, `get_tag()`, `is_tag_closer()`, and `serialize_token()` for opener, text, child opener, child text, child closer, and parent closer.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state that closers are emitted for implicitly closed and EOF-unclosed elements, but the rewrite implications are not highlighted near the serialization guidance.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a rewrite note that virtual closers should be handled by the same opener/closer boundary rule as source closers, and that an element closed by EOF is not necessarily an incomplete syntax token.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn that `normalize($html)` starts over from original bytes, but candidates still used it as a recovery path after building a rewritten output.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Separate unsupported-parser fallback from best-effort incomplete-input policy, and state that normalizing the original input intentionally restores any tokens skipped or replaced during the rewrite.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs show return values, but not the common rewrite idiom that matching a tag name during `next_token()` catches both opener and closer while returning `null` for text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an opener/closer example under token walking that demonstrates `if ( 'X' === $processor->get_tag() ) { continue; }` as a boundary-token filter, and explain when an explicit `get_token_type() === '#tag'` guard is optional.
